question.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.

We begin by performing the operations inside the parentheses. So, first we multiply $(-4)$ by $7$:

$$
\begin{aligned}(32+(-4)\times 7)^{3} & =(32+(-28))^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we add the numbers inside the parentheses: 

$$
\begin{aligned}(32+(-28))^{3} & ={4}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the exponent:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{3}=64\end{aligned}
$$
